{{Quote|The system is called Yavin on our charts, Dark Lord... It appears perfect&mdash;isolated, uninhabited. We will never be found.|A Sith navigator to Naga Sadow|<ref name="TFotSE5">[[Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire 5|''Tales of the Jedi – The Fall of the Sith Empire'' 5]]</ref>}}
The '''Yavin system''' was a three-[[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Star system/Legends|star system]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] that contained the [[Gas giant/Legends|gas giant]] [[Yavin Prime/Legends|Yavin Prime]] and its twenty-six [[Moon/Legends|moons]]; only three of which were habitable: [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]], [[Yavin 8/Legends|Yavin 8]], and [[Yavin 13/Legends|Yavin 13]]. Discovered by [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] [[Scout/Legends|scouts]] during the [[Expansionist Period/Legends|Expansionist Era]], this overall inhospitable star system went down in history millennia later during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], when it hosted the famous [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]].
In the decades following the end of the conflict, the Yavin system was passed down from hand to hand, conquered by [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] warlords, before being recaptured by the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] and colonized by the [[Extragalactic/Legends|extra-galactic]] invaders known as the [[Yuuzhan Vong]].

Despite its reputedly inhospitable environment, the Yavin system was home to at least four sapient native species, namely the [[Melodie]]s, the [[Gerb]]s, the [[Slith]]s, and a [[Tarron Neb's species|race]] of [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] that was wiped out by the Galactic Empire. Additionally, Yavin 4 became an adopted home for several other species, including the [[Critokian]]s, the [[Massassi/Legends|Massassi]] [[Sith (species)/Legends|Sith]], and some [[Human/Legends|Humans]].

==Description==
{{Quote|The fourth moon appears habitable, Dark Lord... Covered with jungle... lush with life.|A Sith navigator|<ref name="TFotSE5" />}}
[[File:YavinPrime-AORCR.png|thumb|left|250px|Yavin Prime with its many moons]]
The Yavin [[Star system/Legends|system]] was part of the [[Gordian Reach/Legends|Gordian Reach]], a [[Sector/Legends|sector]] of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]].<ref name="TEA" /> It consisted of a medium-sized [[Color/Legends|orange]] [[Star/Legends|star]] with three [[Planet/Legends|worlds]] orbiting it. The closest to the sun, [[Fiddanl]], was a barren planet covered with mercury seas and instable landmasses. The second orbit was occupied by [[Stroiketcy]], a captured [[Comet/Legends|comet]], and the last planet in the system was [[Yavin Prime/Legends|Yavin Prime]], a red [[Gas giant/Legends|gas giant]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide 2" />

While none of the planets were habitable, twenty-six [[Moon/Legends|moons]] orbited Yavin Prime, the largest three of which were hospitable. [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]] hosted a great variety of [[Plant/Legends|flora]] and fauna in tropical jungles, [[Yavin 8/Legends|Yavin 8]] was covered in tundras and mountains, while [[Yavin 13/Legends|Yavin 13's]] terrain consisted mostly of rocky plains and deserts.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 2" /> Throughout history, a number of [[Space station/Legends|space stations]] were also established within the boundaries of the system, most of them orbiting around the gas giant.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 2" /><ref name="Young Jedi Knights: Heirs of the Force" /><ref name="Star Wars Galaxies" /><ref name="Knights of the Old Republic" />

Although not a part of it, a dense, purple [[Nebula/Legends|nebula]] was also located in the vicinity of the Yavin system. This interstellar cloud was christened "[[Shadow of the Alliance]]" during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]],<ref name="SWGCG" /> a major conflict fought between the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]].<ref name="AGTSWU2">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]''</ref>

Despite its generally inhospitable conditions, the Yavin system hosted at least four native [[Sentience/Legends|sentient]] [[Species/Legends|species]]. The lagomorph [[Gerb]]s and the serpentine [[Slith]] hailed from Yavin 13, while the eighth moon hosted aquatic [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]] known as the [[Melodie]]s,<ref name="Galaxy Guide 2" /> and yet another [[Tarron Neb's species|bipedal species]]. The latter went extinct with the rise of the [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Galactic Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]], who grew disgusted by the Yavin 8 natives and ordered that they be wiped out.<ref name="daa" />

==History==
{{Quote|I'm taking you all the way to the Yavin system, after all. That place is on the left side of nowhere &mdash; why do you idealists pick the worst planets to meet on, anyway?|Han Solo|<ref name="Captive">''[[Star Wars Journal: Captive to Evil]]''</ref>}}
More than [[7,500,000,000 BBY|seven and a half billion]] [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], [[Hydrogen/Legends|hydrogen]], [[Helium/Legends|helium]] and interplanetary dust coalesced to form the Yavin system.<ref name="Formation date">''[[Galaxy Guide 2: Yavin and Bespin]]'' dates the formation of the Yavin system to more than 7,5 billion [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].</ref>

===Ancient history===
{{Quote|A secret place&hellip; for a new start.|Naga Sadow on Yavin 4|<ref name="TFotSE5" />}}
The first known colonists in the Yavin system belonged to the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata's]] [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]] around [[30,000 BBY]]. However, a deadly plague spread among the Rakata in [[25,200 BBY]], and their Empire fractured.<ref name="TEA" /> The system then fell into oblivion and was only rediscovered during the [[Expansionist Period/Legends|Expansionist Era]],<ref name="Galaxy Guide 2" /> which started after the [[Galactic Constitution/Legends|establishment]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] in [[25,053 BBY]].<ref name="SWTOR">{{Holonet|allegiances|galactic-republic|The Galactic Republic}}</ref> As was customary at the time, the name Yavin was given to both the star and the major world in the system. The first exploration report deemed the system unfit for Human colonization and probably devoid of any lifeform, let alone intelligent life. Upon entering the system, the early scouts noticed an orange sun nearing the term of its middle-age cycle. The explorers thought they needed look no further, so they left the system after a brief cursory examination of the planets and moons.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 2" />

Because of its alleged inhospitality, the Yavin system remained a brief footnote in the planetary registries of the Republic for centuries, but Yavin 4 became a [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] stronghold around [[5000 BBY/Legends|5000 BBY]], when the [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Naga Sadow/Legends|Naga Sadow]] went into self-imposed [[Exile (punishment)/Legends|exile]] following his defeat at the [[second battle of Korriban]].<ref name="Galaxy Guide 2" />

===Headquarters of a Rebel Alliance===
{{Quote|You would prefer another target, a military target? Then name the system! I grow tired of asking this so it will be the last time: ''Where'' is the rebel base?|[[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]] to [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]]|<ref name="A new Hope" />}}
[[File:DeathStarYavinSystem-ANH.png|thumb|left|250px|The Death Star approaching Yavin Prime]]
However, the Yavin system remained largely unknown and uncharted until millennia later, when the Rebel Alliance set up a major base in the fourth moon of Yavin Prime.<ref name="Galaxy Guide 2" /> Even at the height of the Galactic Civil War, the system did not appear on many astrogation charts, since it was far from the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] and major [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]]. With the establishment of the Alliance's headquarters on Yavin 4, the star system became the site of the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], during which several Rebel pilots destroyed the Empire's [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station/Legends|first]] [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]].<ref name="SWGCG" />

Following the destruction of their [[Superweapon/Legends|superweapon]], the Empire launched a number of [[Battle of Yavin 4|small raids]] at the Rebel base on Yavin 4, which prompted the Alliance to [[Evacuation of Yavin|evacuate]] the moon to escape retaliation.<ref name="DM">"[[Doom Mission]]"</ref> The Empire officially restricted Yavin 4 space to Imperial traffic, maintaining a heavy military presence that had been maintained within the Yavin system for the remainder of the war.<ref name="SWGCG" />

===A system changing hands===
In the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|aftermath]] of the [[Death/Legends|death]] of [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="SW Episode VI">{{Film|VI}}</ref> the Galactic Empire shattered into several competing [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|factions]]. At the same time, the Rebel Alliance reorganized into the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], a democratic government the function of which was to replace the Empire. Between 4 and [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], the Yavin system remained under the control of the [[Zsinj]], former [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] of the [[Quelii Oversector]] and leader of [[Zsinj's Empire|his own]] faction. Following Zsinj's death, his former rival and fellow Imperial [[Treuten Teradoc]] sought to acquire the Grand Moff's former worlds. However, Teradoc soon found himself caught in a war with [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Gial Ackbar]] of the New Republic, and [[Teren Rogriss]]&mdash;another Imperial who wanted to conquer Zsinj's territory. Teradoc was forced to retreat to the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]]. The Yavin system then fell under the rule of [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]], one of the twelve original [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admirals]] of the Empire, and was now part of [[Thrawn's confederation]]. One year [[9 ABY/Legends|later]], with Thrawn's death, the confederation collapsed, and the system was eventually recovered by the New Republic.<ref name="TEA" />

Between [[26 ABY/Legends|26]] and [[27 ABY/Legends|27 ABY]], the Yavin system was attacked by the extragalactic [[Yuuzhan Vong]], a race of technology-hating [[Alien/Legends|non-Humans]]. The system fell under the control of the invaders and became a part of the [[Yuuzhan Vong empire]].<ref name="TEA" /> However, [[29 ABY/Legends|two years later]], the Empire was destroyed when the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] retook its former [[Capital/Legends|capital]] planet of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] and killed the Vong's [[Supreme Overlord]] [[Shimrra Jamaane]].<ref name="TFU">''[[The New Jedi Order: The Unifying Force]]''</ref> By [[137 ABY]], the system was affiliated with [[Darth Krayt]]'s [[Darth Krayt's Galactic Empire|Sith Empire]].<ref name="TEA" />
